stitch_shortlist.author: abbeyyung
stitch_shortlist.claim: 'My haircare routine gave thousands of you insane hair transformations' (2.9M, 6.9d)

pitch.the_claim: A cosmetic haircare routine (conditioner-heavy, bond builders) turned into 'insane hair transformations' for followers — implying routine = hair growth.
pitch.why_it_stitches: 2.9M in 6.9d (424K/day), 1K comments, and a follow-up 'yes I use a LOT of conditioner' at 283K in 2.9d — the biggest hair wave in the window; half-right: routine changes shine, breakage and length retention, not follicle growth. Miss recorded: 6.9d, no longer rising (a week old — stitch it as the peg for the minoxidil answer card, not as a fresh react). Lane call: cosmetic hair, not derm — doubt stated, but hair is her underexploited lane.
pitch.your_fit: Corpus yellow: hair-loss ratings (1.9M TT, Dec 2025 — 'minoxidil 10/10, biotin 0/10, hair serum 7/10'), telogen effluvium guides, 'you're applying minoxidil WRONG' (Mar 2026). No prior video on cosmetic routines vs growth — a NEW angle.
angles: 'yes, and': shine and length retention are real — growth is a follicle problem, and here's how to tell which one you have
switch-don't-quit: keep the routine, add the two things that actually change density (minoxidil, and ruling out TE)
empathy-first: 'if your hair looks better but isn't thicker, this is why'

stitch_shortlist.claim: Rhinophyma diary — 'raising awareness' of the bulbous-nose rosacea (517K, 3.3d)

pitch.the_claim: A patient documents living with rhinophyma — the thickened, bulbous nose — 'for awareness'; most viewers don't know it's a subtype of rosacea and that it's treatable.
pitch.why_it_stitches: 517K in 3.3d (157K/day — slowed from the 272K/day pace of two days ago, no longer on a 1M track), 263 comments; a patient, so this is empathy-first 'yes, and' only — never a correction. Surprising trigger: viewers assume alcohol; it's rosacea (phymatous), it's treatable, and it's not the patient's fault.
pitch.your_fit: Corpus: rosacea is a doctor-AND-patient topic for her ('When it comes to rosacea, I'm both a doctor and a patient' — 65K TT, Apr 2023; 'I use azelaic acid every single day for my redness and rosacea'). No transcript mentions rhinophyma specifically — the phymatous-subtype facts need her take. Playbook: rosacea (demodex, PDL/IPL related).

stitch_shortlist.claim: Ice cubes on your face — a derm's icing routine (319K, 3.3d)

pitch.the_claim: Rubbing ice cubes on the face (de-puffing, 'tightening', glow) — a derm endorsing the icing trend.
pitch.why_it_stitches: 320K in 3.3d (97K/day), 48s; a fellow derm, so 'yes, and' only: ice does calm transient puffiness and inflammation, but direct ice on skin risks cold injury and flares rosacea/flushing. stitch_shortlist.claim: 5% glutathione + vitamin C serum 'brightens dark areas' (802K, 6.3d)

pitch.the_claim: A 5% glutathione + 2% vitamin C + PHA + HA serum evens out dark areas — 'it smells weird but that's why I trust it'.
pitch.why_it_stitches: 800K in 6.3d (127K/day), 226 comments, hyperpigmentation seed; half-right — vitamin C, PHA and consistency help PIH, but topical glutathione has thin evidence and the 'smell = potency' logic is wrong. stitch_shortlist.claim: 'That hyped hand cream gave me dark knuckles' — dark-knuckle remover (486K, 6.8d)
